Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines · House layout, roofs, rooms & furnishings

picture noun

also pictures, painting, illustration

classical

Cic. Verr. 2.4.1
Sen. Ep. 16.8
Traupman 360

1pictūra: short i (Traupman 360 pīctūra). Lewis & Short leaves the vowel unmarked, as in pictus and pictor; de Vaan 465 sets Proto-Italic *pikto-, painted. The libellī write pictūrās.

pictūra1, pictūrae f.

noun, first declension

picture, painting

The household word: in the libellī the boy ‘reads’ a book by looking at its pictures, pictūrās spectāvit.

Other words

  • imāgō, imāginis f. — image, likeness

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Verg. A. 8.730; Traupman 360

    A likeness of someone or something; the lexicon’s photo is imāgō phōtographica.

  • tabula picta — a painting on a panel

    also used · classical · Cic. Brut. 261 (Lewis & Short, s.v. tabula); M-O s.v. painting; Traupman 168

Examples

  • Theodōrus librum ā patre accēpit, et ōre clausō, oculīs apertīs, pictūrās spectāvit.

    Theo took the book from Dad and, with his mouth shut and his eyes open, looked at the pictures.Libellus VI, Reditus: per Alpēs domum

  • animum pictūrā pāscit inānī

    he feeds his heart on the empty pictureVerg. A. 1.464

  • rērumque ignārus imāgine gaudet

    and, knowing nothing of what it shows, he delights in the pictureVerg. A. 8.730

See also draw, photo, book, paint.

SourcesLewis & Short: pictura · Lewis & Short: imago · Lewis & Short: tabula

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 168, 360. Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. painting.

Michiel de Vaan, Etymological Dictionary of Latin and the other Italic Languages (2008), p. 465, s.v. pingō.

Vergil, A. 8.730, from the Latinitas loci collection (loci-vergilius); A. 1.464 as Lewis & Short quotes it (s.v. pāscō).

Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 9 November 2026. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word.
